proof: A rectangle covers n full bins with edges summing to r, or n-1 full bins with edges summing to 1+r, along each axis.
For fixed perpendicular intersections, excess is convex and symmetric in the two edge fragments, so equal fragments minimize it.
Taking the minimum of the four balanced-edge combinations gives each rectangle's independent minimum; summing and ignoring fixed occupancy is conservative.
Take the maximum of this bound and the existing core-capacity bound. Neither changes target density or raw convergence checks.
